content.content:
# grow_with_claudinite

Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the
existing fleet), and **opt-out by removal**: baselining never re-adds it.

This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.

Its scheduled work is five tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
scheduler (`engine/scheduler/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:

| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | canon changed, or the project's local packs changed (or weekly) | a PR against the repo's `main` |
| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via a reviewed PR |
| `conversation-extract` ([tasks/conversation-extract/task.md](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md)) | after a substantive merge, or to run the retention prune | the repo's own local packs, plus the prune on the logs branch |
| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | daily (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |

A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "grow_with_claudinite", "config": { "promote": false } }`
— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).

## The conversation lifecycle — capture in-session, extract in a daily task, retention

The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions** — the conversation-side sibling of the
issues/PRs/commits extract above, replacing the old in-session post-merge lessons pass. The two
halves split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session transcript, so it runs
in-session (at merge, and again when the session ends); **extraction** only reads the
already-pushed logs, so it is an ordinary
scheduled task with `growth-extract`'s access model — the logs branch is *in the repo*,
so reading it, committing lessons to local packs, and pruning are plain local git on the working
tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the GitHub MCP tools.

1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
   Right after a merge lands:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
   net), and pushes one file per **capture event** onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`**
   branch: `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`.
   **Delta-aware, keyed on the session id:** every capture pushes only the entries after this
   session's previous capture, whatever event produced it, so any two events chain into
   disjoint files and a zero delta pushes nothing at all. Double-writing is therefore safe by
   construction, not by coordination — the property [`session-end.mjs`](session-end.mjs) relies
   on, so `pack.test.mjs` pins it directly.
   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
1. **Capture — again, when the session ends** ([session-end.mjs](session-end.mjs), invoked by the
   engine's SessionEnd hook runner for every active pack that ships one). Same capture, with
   `--issue 0`: **`0` means "no associated issue"**, and the filename shape stays byte-identical
   on purpose — the retention prune, the `conversationLogs` signal and the extract's filename
   parse all already accept it, whereas a *new* shape would be invisible to the prune and become
   immortal on the branch. This event is what captures the sessions that never merge (a review, an
   investigation, a session that ended in a question) and the post-merge **tail** of the ones that
   do. **Best effort:** a container reclaimed by timeout never fires it, so nothing depends on it
   having run — every firing enriches the record, every miss leaves exactly the merge-only
   behaviour. An `issue-0` log has no issue for `conversation-extract` to post its exchange
   summary on; nothing else about its lifecycle differs.
2. **Fresh pass — the [conversation-extract](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md) scheduled task**
   (precondition: a substantive merge, or a logs branch with retention configured so the age-based
   prune still runs on a quiet repo; local git on the
   repo's working tree, MCP only for the issue comment). It applies
   [extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md) (the method — friction signals and the
   measured efficiency analysis, computable from the log's timestamps and token usage), routes
   keepers into the member's local packs, and posts on the worked issue, for each rule that landed,
   a **200-word-max** summary of the slice of conversation that caused it — the dialogue itself is
   never pasted there, it is far too verbose for an issue —
   **extraction is the only path to permanence**: a log that yields no rule gets no comment,
   and its conversation is gone once retention deletes it (a deliberate owner call).
3. **Final pass and deletion** — once a log ages past `config.retention_days`, the same task
   re-reads it with ~a week of hindsight (the rethink window), then deletes it (the weekly full
   sweep guarantees the prune runs even on a repo gone quiet). Every log gets exactly two
   judgment passes. **Unset retention = the prune deletes nothing** (capture-only, fail-safe).

No adoption question over it — `retention_days` stays unset (hidden) by default, which is
fail-safe (capture-only). A project that wants the prune active sets `config.retention_days`
itself (10 is the recommended floor); nothing else to schedule, since extraction rides the
fleet's one daily run like the other growth tasks.

## Skill-usage metrics — what the mounted skills actually do

Mounting a skill only puts its name and one-line description into the session prompt; whether the
model ever **loads** it is discretion, and nothing recorded it. So the promotion ladder's
skill-vs-prose call had no empirical feedback: a skill whose trigger never fires looked exactly like
one that fires daily, and a "skill" that loads in every session (rules wearing a skill's clothes)
looked exactly like a genuinely activity-scoped one.

The [usage-fold](tasks/usage-fold/task.md) task closes that loop — daily, agentless, seconds. It
counts skill loads **and their denominators** (captures, merges, sessions, user messages, user
commands) out of the logs this pack already captures, into
`.claudinite/local/usage.GENERATED.json`: day rows recomputed statelessly inside the raw retention
window, week rows appended once past a `foldedThrough` watermark. Denominators are the point — a raw
count cannot tell healthy-rare from broken, so the question is loads *against the sessions where that
skill's own declared trigger plausibly applied*. Zeros are implicit (a skill with no loads has no
key), which is what makes "never loads" visible: diff the file against the repo's mounted skills.

Fleet-wide aggregation is deliberately **not** here — the canon knows mechanisms, never repos. It is
the sheepdog pack's [`fleet-usage`](../sheepdog/tasks/fleet-usage/task.md) task, in the fleet-enforcer
repo, which is the only place that knows who the members are.

## Rules

| Rule | Kind | What |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-config` | hardcoded ([config-check.mjs](config-check.mjs)) | entry config shape valid |

**Pack discovery** ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) is
an ordinary weekly task on the repo's own scheduler. The repo runs the whole pipeline over
**itself**: manifest its stack, hold it against the canon packs already on its shelf and its own
existing local packs, and — for genuinely project-specific knowledge neither homes — author a new
**local** pack populated from its real usage, landed through a **reviewed** PR (a new pack ships new
`.mjs` checks, and a check can break CI — the same reason `prose-to-checks-sweep` is reviewed, and
the one place this stage differs from extract). It writes only the repo's own
`.claudinite/local/packs/`; lifting a local pack up into the shared canon is the central promote
task's job.

## Identifying a project's capture surface: its local packs (the same way in every stage)

Every growth stage operates on a project's **local packs** — the tracked packs a repo keeps under
`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/` (prose in `RULES.md`, checks in the pack's `rules`, activity
procedures as the pack's skills, scheduled tasks under its `tasks/`). That subtree **is** the
project's own content;

lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.

This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.

Its scheduled work is five tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
scheduler (`engine/scheduler/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:

| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | canon changed, or the project's local packs changed (or weekly) | a PR against the repo's `main` |
| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via a reviewed PR |
| `conversation-extract` ([tasks/conversation-extract/task.md](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md)) | after a substantive merge, or to run the retention prune | the repo's own local packs, plus the prune on the logs branch |
| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | daily (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |

A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "grow_with_claudinite", "config": { "promote": false } }`
— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).

## The conversation lifecycle — capture in-session, extract in a daily task, retention

The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions** — the conversation-side sibling of the
issues/PRs/commits extract above, replacing the old in-session post-merge lessons pass. The two
halves split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session transcript, so it runs
in-session (at merge, and again when the session ends); **extraction** only reads the
already-pushed logs, so it is an ordinary
scheduled task with `growth-extract`'s access model — the logs branch is *in the repo*,
so reading it, committing lessons to local packs, and pruning are plain local git on the working
tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the GitHub MCP tools.

1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
   Right after a merge lands:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
   net), and pushes one file per **capture event** onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`**
   branch: `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`.
   **Delta-aware, keyed on the session id:** every capture pushes only the entries after this
   session's previous capture, whatever event produced it, so any two events chain into
   disjoint files and a zero delta pushes nothing at all. Double-writing is therefore safe by
   construction, not by coordination — the property [`session-end.mjs`](session-end.mjs) relies
   on, so `pack.test.mjs` pins it directly.
   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
1. **Capture — again, when the session ends** ([session-end.mjs](session-end.mjs), invoked by the
   engine's SessionEnd hook runner for every active pack that ships one). Same capture, with
   `--issue 0`: **`0` means "no associated issue"**, and the filename shape stays byte-identical
   on purpose — the retention prune, the `conversationLogs` signal and the extract's filename
   parse all already accept it, whereas a *new* shape would be invisible to the prune and become
   immortal on the branch. This event is what captures the sessions that never merge (a review, an
   investigation, a session that ended in a question) and the post-merge **tail** of the ones that
   do. **Best effort:** a container reclaimed by timeout never fires it, so nothing depends on it
   having run — every firing enriches the record, every miss leaves exactly the merge-only

   and its conversation is gone once retention deletes it (a deliberate owner call).
3. **Final pass and deletion** — once a log ages past `config.retention_days`, the same task
   re-reads it with ~a week of hindsight (the rethink window), then deletes it (the weekly full
   sweep guarantees the prune runs even on a repo gone quiet). Every log gets exactly two
   judgment passes. **Unset retention = the prune deletes nothing** (capture-only, fail-safe).

## Task to execute

This is the "growth-dedup" task from the `grow_with_claudinite` pack: it prunes this repo's own **local packs** where the shared **canon** it consumes now covers the same point, and opens a PR against `main` for human review.

## Binding context for this run

- **This repo IS the Claudinite canon itself** — it dogfoods its own growth pipeline. So for this run:
  - "the repo's own local packs" (the prune target) = everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (currently two packs: `claudinite` and `canon-curation`).
  - "the mounted canon" (the yardstick you prune against) = this repo's own canon proper, i.e. everything under `packs/`, `skills/`, `engine/` etc. at repo root — NOT a separate vendored mount (there is no `.claudinite/shared/` here since this repo IS the canon). Wherever the task file says "the mounted canon" or references `.claudinite/shared/engine/...`, substitute the root-level equivalent in this repo, e.g. the conformance-check catalog is `node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list` (verified working from repo root).
- **No Context block was included in the dispatching issue** (issue #546, body was just the task path + slot, no "Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs" narrowing). Per the task file's own rule for this case: compare **every** local item against the **whole** mounted canon — nothing is narrowed.
- **Outcome ceiling: `open-pr`.** You may open at most one PR against `main`. You must NEVER merge it yourself, and NEVER push directly to `main`. If you find nothing to prune, doing nothing (no PR) is a complete success — do not manufacture work.
- **Time budget: 30 minutes** for this run (the dispatch's declared `executionTimeout` is 1800s). If you're going to run long, wrap up what you can respect, and clearly report in your final message what got done vs. not, rather than leaving something half-edited.
- **GitHub access is MCP-only** — use the `mcp__github__*` tools for all issue/PR operations (finding/creating the tracking issue, opening the PR, posting comments). Do not use `gh` or `curl` for GitHub API calls. Plain `git`/local shell is fine for branch, commit, and push operations against this one repo.

## What to report back

In your final message, state plainly:
1. Whether you found anything to prune, and if so, a short list of what/where and the canon citation for each.

1	# Growth — dedup local packs against the canon (per repo)
2	
3	The growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile this repo's **local packs** against the shared **canon** it
4	consumes (Claudinite, vendored read-only), pruning local items — a pack's prose line, or a whole local check —
5	the canon now covers. It opens a PR against the repo's default branch for the owner to approve. Often there's
6	nothing to prune, and that's fine. You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue, whose
7	**Context** is **binding scope — not a hint** (the executor will not let you re-decide or widen it).
8	
9	> This task only prunes local packs against the canon; lifting local items up into the canon is the central
10	> promote task's job (canon-side).
11	
12	## Conventions used in this doc
13	
14	- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
15	- **GitHub access is MCP-native.** Updating the tracking issue and opening the PR go through the session's
16	  **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub access — the shell reaches
17	  only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so never reach for `gh`/`curl` or
18	  a cross-repo clone.
19	- **The mounted canon.** The exact canon revision this repo currently consumes — compare against *that*, not a
20	  live fetch. It is what `.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp (a promotion is visible here only
21	  once baselining has converged the mount to include it). Prune only against what the repo actually mounts.
22	- **The dispatch's Context narrows the *yardstick*, never the local surface.** When the Context names
23	  newly-changed canon packs ("Re-check local items against these newly-changed canon packs: …"), **those packs
24	  are this run's entire yardstick**: every prune must cite a line or rule id from one of *them*, and you never
25	  widen the comparison to the rest of the mounted canon. What is *not* narrowed is the local side — **every**
26	  local item is in play against those packs, whatever it is about. (Local pack names are unrelated to canon
27	  pack names, so there is nothing to match up.) A dispatch with **no** Context block carries no such bound: the
28	  precondition emits the list only when the mounted canon moved, and its other arm — the repo's own local packs
29	  changed — deliberately emits none, so that run compares the fresh local items against the whole mounted canon.
30	- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) —
31	  everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the
32	  rename window). That's the corpus this task prunes within; the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under
33	  `.claudinite/` is never a prune target, only the yardstick you prune *against*.
34	
35	## What it does: prune / rephrase local packs the canon now covers
36	
37	When the canon has **absorbed** a practice a local doc still carries — most often an item the central promote
38	task lifted up and the canon now owns — the local copy is redundant. This task:
39	
40	- **Removes** the now-duplicated local item, since the canon is the single source of truth for portable rules.
41	- **Strips** a *partially* covered item down to its residue — when an item's general half is now canon-owned
42	  but it still carries a stronger point about a narrower case, **delete the portable half in place and keep
43	  only the residue**. A strip is a **deletion that shrinks the entry**: lead with the residual point (using the
44	  file's own `(canon)` tag convention if it has one), never with a meta-line like "this rule is portable
45	  (canon)", and **never re-state the now-canon rule, its fix, or which pack owns it** — carrying it is exactly
46	  what you are removing. If your "strip" adds words or restates the canon, you have *un*-deduped the item: keep
47	  the pre-edit text instead.
48	- **Rephrases** a local procedure *only* when the canon's wording of the same idea has changed, so the local
49	  packs stay consistent with the canon they point at — a rephrase tracks a wording drift; it never grows the
50	  entry and never re-imports canon prose.
51	
52	**Keep a local item only if it says *more* than the canon — not merely says it more specifically.** Every
53	local item is more specific than the canon, so specificity alone is never the test. Distinguish two cases:
54	
55	- **The general rule in local dress** — it makes the canon's point but leans on this repo's classes, files, or
56	  names to make it. Once the canon covers the point, those names were only illustration: prune it.
57	- **A stronger point about a narrower case** — it asserts something the canon's general rule leaves out: a
58	  tighter constraint, a sharper claim that holds for this repo's narrower situation. Keep it.
59	
60	So ask not "is it specific" (it always is) but "does it only lean on specific names to make the general point,
61	or does it make a point the canon doesn't?" Prune the first; keep the second.
62	
63	## A canon check covers an item too — and more strongly than prose
64	
65	The canon carries rules as **conformance checks**, not only prose. A local item is covered when a canon check
66	*enforces* it — stronger coverage than a stated line, since the rule runs on every session and CI pass.
67	Consult the machine-readable rule catalog (`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`:
68	id, severity, description, doc pointer — it lists the active local packs' own checks too) alongside the prose
69	corpus, and when a check covers the item, **quote the rule id** where you'd otherwise quote a canon line. This
70	cuts both ways: a **local pack's own check** is redundant once a canon check enforces the same rule — prune the
71	local `.mjs` (and drop it from `pack.mjs` + its fixture) exactly as you'd prune a duplicated prose line. The
72	keep-test above is unchanged: a local item that says *more* than the check detects (a stronger point about a
73	narrower case) stays.
74	
75	## Discipline
76	
77	- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon line (or the
78	  covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson.
79	- **Open a single PR against `main`** from a per-run-unique branch (see
80	  [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md)) — one PR for the
81	  whole run's prunes, not one per item — never a direct push. This is an unattended task, on a capable model, and a **wrongful prune
82	  deletes a real local lesson**, so — unlike [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md), whose additive edits
83	  ride a PR that auto-merges after CI — this task keeps a **human** approval gate (its declared outcome ceiling
84	  is `open-pr`: it may open a PR but never merge it). **Put the issue reference in the commit message** —
85	  `Refs #<n>` for this task's tracking issue (below), in the commit itself, not only the PR body. The repo's
86	  `basics` `task-lifecycle` check gates a PR on its commits referencing an issue, so a prune commit that cites
87	  none reds the repo's CI and blocks the merge.
88	- If an edit touches something a test reads, run the repo's offline test suite and keep it green before pushing.
89	
90	## Tracking
91	
92	The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:
93	
94	> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Dedup**
95	
96	Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**. A run that finds no issue under
97	the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open, close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no
98	meaning, only the log does. Log each run that changed a doc as a **dated comment** — naming what was pruned and
99	the canon line that now covers it. A run that prunes nothing logs nothing.
100	
101	## Run on a capable model
102	
103	Proving the mounted canon genuinely covers a local item before pruning it — and telling "the canon now owns
104	this" from "the canon states this too generally, keep the local cut" — is a **judgment call**. A downgraded
105	model prunes a real lesson; the review PR is a backstop, but a wrongful prune is easy to wave through in
106	review, so don't lean on it. This task declares `agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
107	
108	## What this task must never do
109	
110	- **Never edit the read-only canon** — it only prunes the repo's *local packs* against it.
111	- **Never merge its own PR** — the human approval gate is the whole point (`outcome: open-pr`).
112	- **Never prune a local item without quoting the mounted-canon line (or covering check rule id) that covers
113	  it** — when unsure, leave it.
114	- **Never widen the dispatch's Context.** If it named the changed canon packs, a prune citing coverage from
115	  any *other* canon pack is out of scope for this run — leave the item; the cycle that moves that pack will
116	  reach it.
117	- **Never prune a local item that makes a stronger point about a narrower case** than the canon — that isn't
118	  redundancy. (A local item that only restates the canon in repo-specific names *is* prunable once the canon
119	  covers the point.)
120	- **Never let a dedup edit grow an entry or re-import canon prose.** Every action this task takes *removes*
121	  portable text: a Remove deletes the item, a Strip deletes its portable half, a Rephrase tracks a wording
122	  drift without adding. An edit that leaves an entry the same size or larger, re-quotes the now-canon rule, or
123	  names the owning pack's fix is a **corruption, not a dedup** — the exact inverse of the job. When in doubt
124	  about a kept item, leave it byte-for-byte unchanged rather than "reconcile" its wording. The
125	  `dedup-prune-integrity` check (`basics`-style work-scope rule, this pack) is the backstop: it reds the
126	  session when a dedup-labeled commit grows a local-pack prose file, or when any change adds a line that
127	  restates a canon rule ("… is portable (canon)", "… pack owns …").

2	
3	This is the Claudinite home repo's own local pack: the capture surface for lessons that are
4	**specific to working on the canon itself** and would not make sense mounted into a consuming
5	project. Portable lessons — anything true for repos beyond this one — belong in the shared canon
6	under `packs/`/`skills/` instead (proposed by PR, or lifted by the promote stage).
7	
8	The growth lifecycle writes here automatically: the `growth-extract` and `conversation-extract`
9	daily tasks route the canon's own non-portable lessons into this pack (each at the local
10	promotion ladder's strongest mechanism — a check where the rule is deterministic, otherwise terse
11	prose below).
12	
13	## Standing owner decisions — settled, do not re-litigate
14	
15	- **`canon-curation` lives in `.claudinite/local/packs/`, not `packs/`** (owner decision,
16	  2026-07-19). The canon home's curation duties are Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite —
17	  project-specific content on the home's own capture surface. Do not propose moving it back, and
18	  do not describe the move as open or provisional.
19	- **Local-pack `run_daily` scheduling is ON — the fleet's default path** (same decision). The
20	  planner reads every member's local-pack daily descriptors by default; never reintroduce an
21	  "experimental / not enabled" framing or an opt-in seam for it.
22	- **Packs-tree segregation is barriers configuration only.** Any rule about what the `packs/`
23	  tree may reference is expressed by declaring/configuring the `barriers` pack (contributed
24	  edges, `siblings`/`scope` capabilities — extend barriers generically if a capability is
25	  missing). Never write standalone code that checks packs-tree segregation.
26	- **A `docs/<initiative>/DESIGN.md` records the mechanism only** (owner decision, 2026-07-23,
27	  #420). Status, phase tracking, in-flight-PR reconciliation and remaining work live in that
28	  initiative's tracking issue (agent-preprocessing → #394); a phased plan lives in the sibling
29	  `MIGRATION.md`. Don't reintroduce a status / open-questions / remaining-work section there.
30	- **Multi-session work hands off through the tracking issue, never a prepared prompt** (owner
31	  correction, 2026-07-23). The owner's opener is `continue work on #<n>`, so state not written
32	  into the issue is lost. Before ending a session on unfinished work, update the issue and let
33	  the session summary be a pointer to it — never compose a bespoke "pick up from here" prompt.
34	- **The canon never knows which repos consume it — fleet-wide aggregation is Sheepdog's domain**
35	  (owner correction, 2026-07-28, #520). Designing anything that spans repos, the tempting shape is
36	  a member list (or a "fleet" task) living in the canon. It doesn't go here: the canon carries only
37	  **mechanisms exercised on itself**, and the knowledge of *which* repos exist stays in the
38	  **Sheepdog** repo and its pack, which enumerates members at runtime from its own
39	  `.claudinite-checks.json` entry — exactly where `fleet-census` and `fleet-freshness` already keep
40	  it. So a cross-repo feature splits in two: a self-contained per-repo half in the canon, and the
41	  aggregation half as a Sheepdog fleet task. **No repo list exists anywhere in canon code** — and a
42	  derived fleet artifact lands in Sheepdog as a daily **auto-merged PR of a `GENERATED` file**,
43	  never a direct commit to its `main`.
44	- **A pack default stays in the pack — don't ask it at adoption, don't write it into a member's
45	  config** (owner ruling, 2026-07-28, #527/#528). An adoption question whose recommended answer is
46	  right for nearly everyone is "bad noise": it taxes every adopting repo to re-state the default,
47	  and materializing that answer into `.claudinite-checks.json` freezes a copy that then drifts from
48	  the pack and has to be migrated. Keep the default in the pack's own code, ask nothing, and let the
49	  rare project that wants to differ add the setting by hand. Read config as *optional* — an unset
50	  key means "the default", never "misconfigured" (`retention_days` unset is precisely why the
51	  conversation-extract prune is skipped rather than failing).
52	
53	## Canon-specific gotchas
54	
55	- **Baselining backfill skips the home — hand-declare fleet-seeded packs here.** The nightly
56	  baselining that lands a `seededByDefault` pack (and canon-delivered declaration changes) on
57	  every member is gated `!isHome`, so the canon home is the one repo it never reaches: a newly
58	  seeded pack does *not* arrive here automatically — the home's own `.claudinite-checks.json`
59	  must be updated by hand in the same change that flips the seed. The natural drift-guard (a
60	  future check, once the home is clean) is: the home declares every `seededByDefault` non-local
61	  pack.
62	- **The home doesn't declare `git-github`, so its skills never mount — never conclude "no such
63	  skill" from `.claude/skills/`.** `mount-skills.mjs` filters on the *literal* declaration
64	  (`isActive(p, { packs: declared })`), not the `requires` closure `check_the_world.mjs` resolves,
65	  and the baselining that would normalize that closure into `.claudinite-checks.json` is the one
66	  thing gated `!isHome` — so `merge-to-main` and `git-github-advanced` are simply absent here.
67	  Read `packs/<pack>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` out of the tracked tree — the corpus *is* this repo,
68	  and an unmounted skill says nothing about whether its procedure applies. The seed-based
69	  drift-guard above would not catch this (`git-github` arrives by closure, never
70	  `seededByDefault`); a real one compares `resolveDeclaredPacks` against the literal declaration.
71	- **Never re-serialize a repo's JSON config to apply an edit — patch the text.** A round-trip
72	  rewrites what it wasn't asked to: Python's `json.dump` defaults to `ensure_ascii=True` (every
73	  non-ASCII character becomes a `\uXXXX` escape), and indent, key order and the trailing newline
74	  become the serializer's opinion. Nothing fails and tests stay green, so it rides onward. Edit
75	  JSON as anchored text; if you must round-trip, pin every lossy default and read the resulting
76	  diff before committing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `repo-text-sweeps`, where a
77	  `\uXXXX`-in-tracked-JSON check would carry it.)
78	- **Test git fixtures must commit with signing off.** `engine-tests/helpers.mjs`'s `makeRepo`
79	  overrides identity but not signing, so all 31 call sites route fixture commits through the
80	  signing service; when it degrades, each commit blocks on it and the suite leaks descriptors
81	  (~800 per full run against a 4096 cap) until `git commit` and `git push` fail process-wide.
82	  Commit with `git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --no-gpg-sign`: signing a tmpdir throwaway
83	  buys nothing. (Portable — a promote candidate for `writing-tests`.)
84	- **A canon session with a consumer repo also in its sources will reach for the *consumer's*
85	  merge skill — merge by the skill of the repo you are merging into.** Canon work is routinely
86	  dual-repo (the canon plus the fleet member being piloted), and both repos ship a merge skill
87	  under different names — the canon's `packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/` and, say, GCEC's
88	  local `merge-and-ci`. The consumer's skill wins the match on name/description and is followed
89	  to the letter, so the canon-only steps in *its* recipe are silently skipped — repeatedly, the
90	  **post-merge conversation capture** (`node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue
91	  <n>`, the "After the merge" section of `merge-to-main`). So: before merging in a dual-repo
92	  session, resolve the merge skill **by target repo**, not by which skill matched first — and
93	  treat capture as part of the merge, not as an optional epilogue.
94	- **Fail-soft SessionStart steps hide their own breakage fleet-wide — test the emitted
95	  output, not the exit code.** Every `engine/pack_loader/` SessionStart step
96	  (`inject-pack-prose.mjs`, `mount-skills.mjs`, `env-requirements.mjs`) wraps its body in
97	  `try { ... } catch {}` so a broken loader never blocks a session. That fail-soft is deliberate,
98	  but it means a runtime fault — a wrong dynamic-import target, a renamed module — exits 0 and
99	  simply emits nothing: no error, no signal. And because the engine is vendored verbatim into
100	  every member, one canon regression silently disables that step across the whole fleet at once.
101	  So a step like this must be guarded by a regression test that runs the real script against a
102	  real corpus and asserts the **positive** effect — prose IS emitted — never merely that
103	  `status === 0` (which fail-soft makes meaningless); see
104	  `engine-tests/pack_loader/inject-pack-prose.test.mjs`.
105	- **The nightly self-refresh cannot repair the vendor-set computation — pin operational
106	  files against the REAL canon tree.** Baselining's converge re-runs
107	  `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs` from canon HEAD, so a bug *in that computation* is
108	  the one class of canon regression that is not self-healing: every refresh faithfully
109	  reproduces it, and recovery is an out-of-band vendor refresh applied to each member by
110	  hand. So when the vendor set excludes by *pattern*, an operational file that matches
111	  needs a by-path whitelist (`VENDORED_ENGINE_DOCS`) **and** a regression test asserting
112	  against the real canon tree, not only a synthetic fixture: a fixture keeps proving the
113	  whitelist mechanism works while the live path silently drops out from under it (see the
114	  paired tests in `vendoring/compute-vendor-set.test.mjs`).
115	- **You cannot force a due slot by running the scheduler workflow by hand.** Dueness is
116	  stateless — a slot is due iff its time falls in `(last successful run, now]` — so a
117	  `workflow_dispatch` run outside the slot's window succeeds, prints `- no tasks due`, and
118	  does nothing. It looks like a healthy run. To exercise a task Action-side, invoke its
119	  worker directly, or move the slot hour in `taskScheduler` and wait for the cron.
120	- **A scheduled task is gated twice — prove a change through `planRun`, never through its own
121	  precondition.** `planRun` computes the due list *before* any precondition runs, so a task whose
122	  most-recent slot has already been run is never evaluated and never reads its signals at all. #513's
123	  forced-run override landed with every test driving the precondition (or the signal collector) directly
124	  and was inert on exactly the run it existed for — the mid-day manual trigger — because the due-list
125	  gate it never touched had already dropped the task (`evaluations: []`; fixed in #516). A test that
126	  starts *inside* the gate proves only "works once evaluated" and says nothing about whether the task
127	  ever gets there. Drive the real `planRun` from a deliberately **non-due** slot: that is the only shape
128	  that catches it.
129	- **Every due task in a run shares ONE checkout — an agentless worker must not touch it.** The
130	  scheduler runs the whole due list in a single working tree, so a worker that checks out a branch or
131	  leaves an index behind hands the next task a tree it did not expect, and a run that dies leaves the
132	  mess for whatever follows. A task whose output is a regenerated file lands it through
133	  `engine/scheduler/deliver-generated.mjs` — git plumbing against the fetched base tip, with HEAD, the
134	  index and the working tree untouched — and reads its prior state from that base rather than local
135	  HEAD, so stacked runs stay idempotent. (`basics/baselining`'s own deliver is the deliberate
136	  exception: it commits a whole working tree under the member's delivery preference.)
137	- **A code-search hit is evidence; a code-search miss is not — survey by reading each file.**
138	- **Derive the test file list from the tree — every hand-written glob here under-runs the suite.**
139	  There is no `package.json` and no test script, so each session invents its own incantation and
140	  silently verifies less than it thinks. Measured in this checkout: `node --test <dir>` does not
141	  recurse — it resolves the path as a module and dies with `Cannot find module`; bash `**` is not
142	  recursive without `globstar`, so `engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs-tests/**/*.test.mjs` reaches
143	  **37 of 65** tracked test files. Four consecutive sessions (2026-07-26, #459/#452/#435/#468) each
144	  wrote a different command and reported 587, 690, 621 and 697 tests — three of them pushed after
145	  running a strict subset. Neither published list is authoritative either: `ci.yml`'s `tests=(…)`
146	  array omits `vendoring/*.test.mjs`, and `engine/checks/README.md`'s "as CI runs it" one-liner
147	  names `engine/test/`, `skills/` and `mount/`, none of which exist. So enumerate from git and let
148	  the count speak: `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')`. (The drift-guard, once the array is
149	  clean: assert every tracked `*.test.mjs` is matched by `ci.yml`'s globs.)
150	- **A branch that waited overnight has lost its base *and* possibly its premise — re-verify the
151	  problem still exists on current `main`, unasked.** This repo merges its own scheduled-task PRs
152	  without a human, on top of multi-phase migrations that retire whole directories: measured on
153	  PR #465, `main` moved **14 commits in 13.7 hours** and one of them (#473, "retire `run_daily/`")
154	  *deleted the file the PR's diagnosis rested on* and had already landed most of its content. The
155	  branch rebased cleanly and the tests stayed green — the change was simply no longer the change to
156	  make, and the correct move was `git checkout -B <branch> origin/main` and re-applying only the
157	  surviving slice (9 files → 2). So syncing the base is not the check; the check is a **content**
158	  one: after `git fetch`, read what the new commits did to the surface you are changing and state
159	  whether the problem is still there, what the goal was, and what survives. Do this whenever you
160	  return to a paused branch, before presenting it — the owner should never have to ask "is this
161	  change still needed" (asked three times on #465 before it was volunteered).
162	- **`subscribe_pr_activity` blocks for minutes — subscribe once, and never as a way to "wait for
163	  CI".** It reads like a cheap registration, so a session calls it, gets no answer, and calls it
164	  again on the same PR. Measured in the #520 session (`2026-07-28T2208Z`): two consecutive calls on
165	  PR #524 cost **237s + 220s**, and a `send_later` check-in a further **101s** — **558s of that
166	  session's 841s of total tool wall-clock (66%)**, all pure idle, in a session whose actual work was
167	  153 tool calls. One subscription per PR is all there is to gain; a second adds nothing but the
168	  wait. When what you actually want is "is it green yet", read the check status directly and merge
169	  on the already-green result — don't buy the same notification twice.
170	- **The home has no `.claudinite/shared/` mount — machinery paths must accept both roots.** A
171	  consumer runs the vendored engine under `.claudinite/shared/engine/…` with packs under
172	  `.claudinite/(shared|local)/packs/…`; the home *is* the corpus and runs the same code from the
173	  repo root. So a path, regex, or workflow command written to the consumer mount shape works
174	  fleet-wide and fails on exactly this repo — the last place anyone exercises it, so the break
175	  surfaces late. Write the two-root form up front: make the `.claudinite/(shared|local)/` prefix
176	  optional in a pattern, and in a command probe for `.claudinite/shared/` first, falling back to
177	  the repo root.
178

content.content:
1	# canon-curation
2	
3	Claudinite's own curation duties — the fleet-facing work only **Claudinite** runs: promoting
4	members' lessons into the shared canon, sweeping the fleet's stacks for technologies the canon does
5	not yet home, and policing the corpus's `packs/` tree. (The
6	prose-to-checks backlog sweep is no longer canon-only — it moved to
7	[grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md) as a per-repo task with a
8	`pack_paths` config, so every repo sweeps its own packs and Claudinite also its core `packs/`.) A
9	**local pack** of the canon home
10	(`.claudinite/local/packs/`, by owner decision 2026-07-19: Claudinite-maintaining-Claudinite is
11	project-specific content, so it lives on the home's own capture surface, not in the portable
12	canon): `detect: null`, never seeded by `--init` or any migration, declared by hand in exactly one
13	repo — the canon home itself, as `local/canon-curation`. Its `tasks/<name>/` folders are found by
14	the home repo's own scheduler exactly like a canon pack's.
15	
16	**Declaration cardinality is the mechanism.** A pack's tasks run once per *declaring* repo, so a
17	pack only the home repo declares yields exactly one dispatch per task per slot — "central, once"
18	with no bespoke orchestrator step. Un-declaring the pack freezes canon absorption without touching
19	the members' side ([grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md)).
20

22	|---|---|---|
23	| `growth-promote` | a participating member changed its local packs in the window | a PR against Claudinite's `main` |
24	| `growth-discover-packs` | weekly, over every covered member | a PR against Claudinite's `main` |
25	| `migrations-retire` | a fully-applied migration record has passed its TTL | a PR against Claudinite's `main` |

31	
32	- **[tasks/growth-promote/](tasks/growth-promote/task.md)** — the growth lifecycle's central stage: read the changed members'
33	  local packs, **generalize** the portable lessons, route each to the right canon home, and open a
34	  PR for the owner to approve. When a portable lesson's technology has no pack home, it mints a
35	  fingerprinted **stub pack** (in its own dedicated PR). This is the sole judgment gate before
36	  shared canon.
37	- **[tasks/growth-discover-packs/](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)** — the weekly **fleet sweep** for
38	  technologies the canon does not yet home: read every member's stack, fold the members into one view
39	  (so first-sight dedup is free — the third member using a technology is the same gap as the first),
40	  and open an owner-reviewed PR authoring the missing `packs/<tech>/`. Its per-repo namesake in
41	  [grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)
42	  is the other side of that line — it authors a repo's own **local** packs and may never re-create what
43	  a canon pack homes, so only this task can close a canon gap. (Promote's stub-minting is narrower
44	  still: one lesson's technology, minted as a seed; this task authors from the whole fleet's usage.)
45	- **[item-routing.md](item-routing.md)** — the shared worthiness + routing method promote (and an
46	  owner-requested retrospective pass) defers to, so every decision about admitting and placing an
47	  item is made the same way.
48	- **[promote-scope.mjs](promote-scope.mjs)** — the CI write-surface gate on promote's PRs: promote
49	  may write only under `packs/` and `skills/` (keyed on the `growth-promote` branch prefix).
50	
51	## The growth lifecycle — three independent stages, no barriers
52	
53	How a lesson is learned in a consuming project, lifted into the shared canon when it's portable,
54	and pruned back out of the project once the canon owns it. Two packs split it by who declares them:
55	**[grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md)** (member-side: extract + dedup + pack
56	discovery, seeded, opt-out by removal) and **canon-curation** (this pack, the central stage).
57	
58	```
59	EXTRACT   per member    → auto-merging PR against the member's main   (grow_with_claudinite)
60	PROMOTE   central, once → PR against Claudinite's main                (canon-curation)
61	DEDUP     per member    → PR against the member's main                (grow_with_claudinite)
62	```
63	
64	All three are ordinary, **independent** planner units — there is no barrier and no phase ordering.
65	Each stage reads only what is already **merged**: promote processes whatever sits on members' mains
66	when it runs, so a lesson extracted tonight is promoted **tomorrow** night (the extract PR's merge
67	shows up in the next night's local-pack signal), and reaches other members' dedup once the promote PR
68	is approved and merged. That approval was always the dominant latency, so the barrier machinery bought little;
69	if the cadence ever matters, promote can run more often (twice daily, or before and after the
70	nightly) without any design change.
71	
72	**Review gates by blast radius, not uniformly.** Promote opens a PR — it's the sole judgment gate
73	before the shared canon every repo reads, so it always needs a human eye. Dedup opens a PR too — a
74	wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson. Extract lands through an **auto-merging PR** against the
75	member's `main` — it writes only that project's own local packs, so it earns a CI gate and a PR trail
76	but not a human reviewer; auto-merge keeps the fleet's daily lesson-capture from flooding review
77	requests. (An owner-requested, in-session retrospective delivers a PR for a human to review — see
78	[extracting-lessons.md](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/extracting-lessons.md).)
79	
80	**Central execution, no plumbing.** Promote runs from the Claudinite home repo with a fleet-wide
81	token, so it reads every participating member and opens its canon PR directly here — no
82	consumer-side Action, no cross-repo PAT, no labelled-issue up-path. The planner hands its gate the
83	`fleetMembers` aggregate (which members changed, and what they declare), and the gate hands the
84	worker the changed participants as `targets`.
85	
86	The session-scoped sibling of this nightly lifecycle — mining a single working session for lessons
87	— lives with [the growth pack's extracting-lessons method](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/extracting-lessons.md)
88	(applied by its conversation-extract daily task over captured logs), and the member-side method docs
89	(extract, dedup, pack discovery, and how a project's local packs are identified) live with
90	[grow_with_claudinite](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/README.md).

packs/basics/skills/writing-tests/SKILL.md:18:- A test that can only run remotely (e.g. CI-only) must diagnose itself: on failure, dump the observed state, not just an assertion. It must also be *hang-proof* — bound every `await` (a timeout race) and set a test-level timeout — so a failure fails fast with that diagnostic instead of burning the whole job's timeout. An unbounded await on something that never settles (e.g. a callback that silently never fires) turns a 5-second failure into a 20-minute hang, and each CI-only iteration already costs a full round-trip.

1	---
2	name: repo-text-sweeps
3	description: Mechanics for grep/sed sweeps, renames, and path relocations across a repo. Use before a bulk find-replace, a rename, or moving files — and after one, to catch silently broken references.
4	---
5	
6	# Text & file manipulation
7	
8	Portable practices for searching, extracting, and rewriting text across a repository's files — grep/sed sweeps, renames and relocations, and the silent reference-breakage they leave behind. These are project-agnostic; they're the mechanics half of editing a codebase as text. (General software-engineering practices live in [the engineering-practices skill](../engineering-practices/SKILL.md); the merge-time relocation traps — git's rename detection, references that break with no conflict across a merge — live in [the git-github-advanced skill](../../../git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md), "Merging across a file relocation".)
9	
10	- Deleting or renaming a file isn't done until you've grepped the repo for inbound references to it — a removed doc, module, or renamed path leaves dangling links, imports, or index entries behind that no test necessarily catches (e.g. a README docs-index link to a deleted file stays green). Grep the whole tree for the old path right after the removal and fix every hit in the same change.
11	- When you relocate a file's *content or responsibility* into a new home — folding a doc into a pack, moving a function to another module, absorbing a routine into a skill — the original is now **redundant surface**, and reducing it to a tombstone stub (`# retired — see X`) is not finishing the job: the stub still costs a read, drifts from its replacement, and misleads anyone who lands on it. Delete the emptied original in the *same* change, and treat "did this move make anything else dead?" as a standing question after every restructure — the source you copied *from* is the first suspect. Don't wait to be told a leftover is redundant; a relocation that leaves two homes for one thing isn't done.
12	- When renaming `foo/` → `bar/foo/`, a naive repo-wide string-replace of `foo/` → `bar/foo/` causes two silent corruptions: files already under the target namespace double-prefix (`bar/foo/file` → `bar/bar/foo/file`), and external URLs containing the string `foo/` get rewritten. Scope the replace to only internal path strings that need it, or do the replace then make a targeted post-pass reverting matches inside URLs and already-correct paths.
13	- A grep/sed rename pass over a path (`foo/bar/baz.js`) won't match it when built from `path.join` segments (`path.join(__dirname, "foo", "bar", "baz.js")`) or wrapped across a line in a comment — those references survive the rewrite and break only at run time. After a mechanical path-rename pass, also search for the path's individual segment tokens and run the test suite; the test suite, not the grep, surfaces a missed reference.
14	- An ordered specific→catch-all path rewrite can half-convert a reference the specific rule's trailing slash missed. Renaming `old/sub/` → `new/leaf/` with a slash-anchored rule (`s#old/sub/#new/leaf/#`) plus a catch-all for the parent (`s#old/#new/#`), a reference *without* the trailing slash (`path.join(root, "old/sub")`, a bare `git add old/sub`, a prose mention) escapes the specific rule, and the catch-all then rewrites only its **parent** — `old/sub` → `new/sub`, not `new/leaf` — a half-converted path that breaks at run time, not at the rewrite. Match both the slashed and bare forms, then grep the bare-dir form (at a quote / paren / line-end) and run the tests.
15	- After `git mv`, re-read the file at its **new** path before rewriting it — an editing tool that tracks reads by path treats the moved path as never-seen and silently refuses the write, leaving the file stale (a failure that surfaces much later, far from its cause). When the move and the rewrite share a batch of tool calls, check each result individually; a single refused write is easy to miss in a batch.
16	- A Markdown link carries its path **twice** — ``[`old/path.md`](old/path.md)`` holds it in both the bracket label and the parenthesized target — so a sed anchored on the `](href)` form updates the link target but leaves the visible `[display text]` reading the old path, and the doc points right while *reading* wrong. After an href-only sweep, also rewrite the display-text form (both plain `[old/path.md]` and backticked) and grep for the old string to catch the labels the href rule didn't touch.
17	- To exclude a directory's own files from a reference search, filter by file **path**, not `grep -v` on line content: `grep -rn foo/bar | grep -v foo/bar/` (meant to drop the directory's own files) *also* drops every legitimate full-path reference elsewhere, silently undercounting. Exclude by pathspec instead — `git grep -n foo/bar -- . ':(exclude)foo/bar'` — which filters on which file is searched, not on what each matching line happens to contain.
18	- To exclude vendored, synced, or generated files from a **structural** check that walks a tree (an orphan/reachability scan, a doc audit, a lint), derive the file set from git's tracked list (e.g. `git ls-files`) rather than a filesystem walk with a hardcoded path to skip — it can't desync when the artifact moves, and it stays correct when a new ignored directory appears. (Sibling of the pathspec-exclude rule above: that one separates a directory from its own files within a search; this one separates owned content from vendored/generated content.)
19	- A zero-hit grep proves absence only at the case you searched. Code normalizes tokens away from prose case — an uppercase data table (`'KNEW'`), a SCREAMING_SNAKE constant, a lowercased slug — so a case-sensitive `grep knew` finds nothing and reads as "not in the codebase" while the entry sits right there, and a conclusion built on that phantom absence compounds. Before concluding a token is absent, re-run with `-i`; when history should have touched it, `git log -S<token>` is the cross-check that catches the miss.
20	- When writing file content captured from a script or command output, use the `Write` tool directly — never `cp` from an internal Claude Code path (`/root/.claude/projects/...`). The tool-results paths are harness-internal and inaccessible to shell commands; referencing them via Bash triggers a permission prompt. Capture the output in context and pass it to `Write`.
21	
22

1	# Evaluating and routing a new item
2	
3	The shared method for three decisions every proposed addition to this corpus must pass through: **is it worthy** of inclusion at all, **which mechanism** should carry it, and — only for prose — **where does it go**. Any routine or person that adds an item — the [growth promote stage](tasks/growth-promote/task.md), an owner-requested retrospective pass, a hand edit — applies this same protocol, so the decision-making lives here once instead of being re-derived per caller.
4	
5	This is a Claudinite-internal doc used by the growth lifecycle (see [the canon-curation README](README.md)): it is **not** part of the mounted corpus and consuming repos do not `@import` it.
6	
7	An "item" is one **distilled, portable rule** — not a transcript, not a narration of what happened. A candidate still phrased as "here's what we did" has not been distilled yet and is below the bar on form alone, before any of the tests below. This doc picks up once a distilled rule exists and decides its fate.
8	
9	## Worthiness — does it earn a place at all
10	
11	The corpus is read read-only by every consuming repo, so a **duplicative** item (already covered) or an **undistilled** one (a story or a truism, not a rule) pollutes shared canon and costs every future reader. The bar guards against *those* — it is **not** a bar on *scope*: an item useful to only one project today can still earn a place (see Portable). Admit an item only when **all** hold:
12	
13	- **Distilled.** It is a single tight rule in the imperative, not a story, a log, or a restatement of a generic truism.
14	- **Portable — would a *future* project benefit?** Not "useful to every project today." An item can help only **one** project right now and still belong here, so long as another project — **especially one with a similar tech stack or process** — would benefit when it arrives. Being specific to a technology or a process is **not** disqualifying: generalize it and route it to that technology's or practice's home. What disqualifies is leaning on *this* project's non-transferable particulars — a product requirement, or a one-off incident in how it happened to call some API. The test, a genuinely hard one: *if another project with a similar tech stack came along, would it benefit from this?* Yes → portable; only-ever-this-product → local.
15	- **Durable and reusable.** It will still apply on a future, unseen task — not a one-off, not a situational detail, not something already implied by an existing rule.
16	- **Readable through the channel it lands in.** A rule whose premise is that the delivery channel
17	  itself failed cannot be carried by that channel. Promote #497 admitted "the tell that the SessionStart
18	  hook did not fire" as pack prose — and pack prose is what that hook delivers, so in the one situation
19	  the rule describes it is not in context to be read. Detecting a channel's own failure belongs in code,
20	  not in the payload the channel carries; reject such an item here rather than rewording it.
21	- **Not already covered.** The insight does not already exist **anywhere** in the corpus, even worded differently or owned by a different file. This is checked against the *entire* corpus, not just the file it would land in — see [Dedupe against the whole corpus](#dedupe-against-the-whole-corpus).
22	
23	Reject on any miss — but the misses that matter are *undistilled*, *already-covered*, or *genuinely one-off*, not merely *narrow*. When you're torn over a real, non-duplicate rule, lean toward **keeping** it — the goal is a broad library. When you're torn over whether something is a duplicate, or a rule at all, leave it out. The failure to avoid is padding the canon with restatements of what's already there; admitting a narrow-but-reusable rule is not that failure.
24	
25	### Dedupe against the whole corpus
26	
27	Before admitting anything, read across the corpus, not only the file you expect to own the item. The same insight is frequently already present under a different heading or in an adjacent group. If it sharpens an **existing** rule, fold it in with a minimal edit rather than adding a second bullet that says nearly the same thing — and never weaken or restate what is already there in the process.
28	
29	## Mechanism triage — prose is the fallback, not the default
30	
31	A worthy item next descends the **promotion ladder** ([../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md](../../../../engine/checks/DESIGN.md) owns it): platform setting (always paired with its verifying check) → PreToolUse hook → conformance check → skill → prose. The *first* rung that can carry the item wins — a rule about repo state becomes a check whose failure message *is* the lesson; a bad action to prevent becomes a guard; a procedure or knowledge with a nameable trigger becomes (or joins) a skill. Only an item none of those can carry — judgment, in-flight behavior, signature-less knowledge — proceeds to the file routing below, and its landing **names that reason** in the promote log so conversion rates stay auditable.
32	
33	**"No universal signature" alone never routes an item to prose.** A rule converts to a check when a *narrow, file-scoped* signature covers the **grounded cases** — the concrete shapes the rule was distilled from — even though no signature covers every conceivable violation. Gate it relevance-first so it stays inert off-target, and document the genuinely signature-less residue in the rule's own comments as out of scope. The prose rung is only for an item whose grounded cases *themselves* have no reliable signature (pure judgment, runtime/in-flight behavior).
34	
35	## Routing — picking the right file (rung-5 items only)
36	
37	Routing is robust when it keys on **stable file groups**, not on the current roster of individual files (which grows over time). The corpus is organized into a few groups, each with its own selection rule:
38	
39	1. **The practice group** — durable, project-agnostic practices, each file a self-contained, reusable unit of know-how the agent applies whenever its subject comes up (engineering, agentic, git/GitHub, testing, investigation, discipline, architecture), partitioned **by kind of practice** with each file owning one recurring subject cluster. This group spans **two folders that differ only by *when* the rule loads**: `always/` for a rule that applies to essentially every task (the index `@`-imports it, so it's force-loaded every session), and `tasks/` for a subject-gated rule read on demand when its trigger fires. Route in two steps: first match the item's *kind* to the file whose cluster already owns that subject; then keep it in `always/` only if it genuinely isn't tied to one kind of task (the rare case — `always/` stays small), otherwise it belongs in `tasks/`. Read the group's own index (the root `CLAUDE.md`) to find the current owner for a kind — never from memory, since the set of clusters can grow.
40	2. **The per-user group** — interaction preferences and trigger phrases, **one file per person**, named for that person's identity. Route an item of this kind to the file for the user it belongs to; it never goes in the practice group.
41	3. **The per-technology group** — practices specific to one technology, **one file per technology**. Route a technology-specific item to that technology's file. When **no pack homes that technology** (not even a stub), the item doesn't land in a loose doc — it **mints a fingerprinted stub pack** (a `packs/<tech>/`, delivered in its own PR), so the next project on that stack self-declares it; [promote](tasks/growth-promote/task.md)'s stub-minting floor and [the generate-project-instructions skill](../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) own the mechanics.
42	
43	Pick **exactly one** owner. If an item plausibly fits two files, choose the single best one — never split one item across files, and never duplicate it into both. The group decides the *axis* (kind, person, or technology); the file within the group is then the one whose existing scope the item falls squarely inside.
44	
45	### When nothing fits
46	
47	An item that matches **no** existing file is **not** a reject signal by itself — a genuinely new category of lesson is meant to be learnable, so a worthy item that no file owns earns its own file. Resolve it in this order:
48	
49	- **Route into an existing owner** when one genuinely fits — the first choice. If the item belongs to a file's cluster and merely sits slightly off-center, a small stretch toward that owner beats spinning up a new file. A new file is for when no existing file's scope genuinely fits, **not** a way to dodge folding into an existing owner.
50	- **Open a new file** when the item clears the [Worthiness](#worthiness--does-it-earn-a-place-at-all) bar in full — distilled, portable, durable and reusable, and not already covered anywhere in the corpus — **and** no existing file's scope genuinely fits it. That is the whole bar: nothing more is required. Do **not** also demand that you expect the cluster to recur, that forcing the item into the closest file would *distort* it, or default to rejecting when the new-file call is a close one — those extra hurdles are dropped. Creating a file obliges registering it where the corpus is indexed and in any routing table, in the **same** change, so it never lands orphaned (see [Keep the write surface bounded](#keep-the-write-surface-bounded)).
51	
52	The loosening above is **only** to the new-cluster hurdle, never to the per-item bar. An item that misses [Worthiness](#worthiness--does-it-earn-a-place-at-all) — a one-off, non-portable or project-specific, a restatement of a generic truism, or already covered anywhere in the corpus — is rejected whether or not a file already exists for it; for the per-item admission decision, the default-to-reject-when-unsure tiebreak still stands.
53	
54	## Keep the write surface bounded
55	
56	Once worthiness and routing are settled, the edit touches **only** the single owning file: add or sharpen one terse rule in that file's existing voice and format, and change nothing else. Do not "improve" unrelated rules while you are in there. The sole exception is the new-file path above, whose surface is itself bounded to the new file plus its index and routing-table registration.
57

1	# Growth — promote lessons into the canon (the central stage)
2	
3	The [growth lifecycle](../../README.md)'s central stage: read the target members' local packs, lift the portable lessons into the shared canon, and open a PR against the canon's default branch **for the owner to approve**. Declared only by the Claudinite home repo, so it runs **once, centrally**, never per project.
4	
5	You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the exact target members (those whose local packs changed in the window). Work exactly that list — the fleet enumeration already happened in the precondition; **do not enumerate the fleet yourself or widen past the Context**.
6	
7	The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`open-pr`**: promotion is the **judgment gate before shared canon**. It opens a PR and **never arms auto-merge** — the owner approves it. But don't lean on that review as the portability check: [extract](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/tasks/growth-extract/task.md) stays project-specific by design, so it's no second opinion, and the owner can't re-derive every portability call. This task's judgment is the real thing between a bad rule and every project that reads the canon — keep the bar high (dedupe against the whole corpus; default to reject when unsure).
8	
9	## Conventions used in this doc
10	
11	- **GitHub access is MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`). You are outside each member repo — read its files over the API (get-file-contents, never a cross-repo checkout; the sandbox has no cross-repo git). The canon PR is opened over MCP too.
12	- **A member's local packs** are everything under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename window) — its own packs, never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.
13	- **`main`** stands for the canon's default branch.
14	
15	## What each run does
16	
17	### 1. Read the target members' local **packs**
18	
19	For each member named in Context, read its **local packs**. The candidate pool is a local pack's captured knowledge — its `RULES.md` **prose** AND its own **checks** (a `<pack>/*.mjs` rule module — its id, description, and failure message *are* a captured, enforceable lesson; the strongest promotion lifts it to a **canon check**, generalized, reusing the [prose-to-checks](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) mechanics — or to canon prose when it doesn't generalize to a check). **Out of scope, staying put:** a lesson deliberately placed as a **code comment at its call site**, a project's task scripts, product source, and config. Never promote from product source. A genuinely portable rule that looks trapped in a code comment was mis-placed at extract time — leave it for a future extract pass to re-home into a pack. You don't need to tell new from old — the dedup step drops anything the canon already carries. No barrier holds tonight's extracts: read whatever is already **merged** on each member's default branch; anything landing mid-run is tomorrow's input.
20	
21	### 2. Generalize each candidate — *before* judging whether it belongs
22	
23	Generalize first, then decide worthiness — never the reverse. The act of generalizing is itself the portability probe — a rule that goes vacuous when lifted, or only makes sense with its project's context, isn't portable; leave it local. Work the rule standalone (origin naming and grouping carry no weight); strip the project (names, files, example stay in the origin repo — promote the distilled rule only); a **technology** mention isn't a disqualifier (lift it to the broadest scope that stays true — tech-specific is fine, *product*-specific is not); decide tool-vs-process and frame it for that home.
24	
25	### 3. Then judge worthiness — deduped against the *entire* corpus
26	
27	Holding the generalized rule, decide if it earns a place by the bar [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns (don't restate its gates). Lean **inclusive** — keep anything a future project could use — but be strict about **duplication**: dedupe against **every** corpus doc, not only the one you'd expect to own it.
28	
29	### 4. Triage the mechanism, then route
30	
31	- **Descend the promotion ladder first** ([item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md)'s mechanism triage). Prose is the fallback, not the default: a lesson a check can carry is **authored as the check** in this PR — the rule module in the right pack, the failure message carrying the generalized lesson, **plus a fixture test proving it fires** on a violating input and stays quiet on a clean one. When a confident detection-plus-fixture can't be authored unattended, land the lesson as prose **and** open a tagged conformance-backlog issue — never a silently-shipped broken check.
32	- **Route** each prose rule to its **one** owning doc ([item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns the placement); match its voice and format; pick exactly one owner, never split or duplicate.
33	- **A technology with no home → mint a fingerprinted stub pack, in its own PR**, reusing the pack-writing mechanics [the generate-project-instructions skill](../../../../../../packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) owns — `packs/<tech>/` with `pack.mjs` (add the `marker`/`detect` fingerprint when the technology carries a reliable one, else `detect: null`), a `RULES.md` seeded from the lesson, a `README.md`, and its `packs/README.md` index row. A minted pack ships in its **own** PR, split from the run's lesson-promotion PR (a new pack earns its own review surface). Never mint from imagination and never park an empty one to fill later — a pack minted here is populated from the *real, portable lesson* that justified it. Do not pad it with speculative rules no project earned — the "written from imagination, not distilled from worked examples" failure; an ungroundable rule isn't written. (Authoring a *fuller* pack from a technology's usage across the whole fleet — rather than a single lesson — is the per-repo pack-discovery task's job, not this floor's.) The follow-ups a fresh stub invites — enriching it from known best practices, triaging which skills it should require, spinning up dependent/aspect packs — are **not** automated here: note them for the owner and leave them to a later, deliberate pass.
34	- **Write it terse — when + what.** State the relevance (*when* it applies) and the rule (*what* to do); add a *why* only to flag severity, in a few words.
35	- **Bounded write surface — `packs/`/`skills/` only** (CI-enforced on the PR). Edit only the one owning doc — or, for a check-conversion, only the new rule module, its registration in the pack registry, and its fixture test. Don't "improve" unrelated rules while you're in there. The two bounded exceptions (both within `packs/`): the new-doc path [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) owns, and minting a stub pack.
36	- **Open a PR against `main`** on a per-run-unique branch — one PR for the whole run's accepted lessons (a minted stub is the exception: its own PR). Never a direct push. Keep every commit and PR terse. **Put the issue reference in the commit message** (`Refs #<n>` for the tracker below) — the `basics` `task-lifecycle` check reds CI on a promote commit that cites none.
37	
38	### 5. Log the run to the tracker
39	
40	Append a dated comment for every run that promoted at least one lesson, and for any notable rejection.
41	
42	## Tracking issue
43	
44	The standing self-improvement log is the issue titled exactly **`Claudinite tracker: Promote to Canon`**.
45	
46	- **Find it by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle).
47	- **Create it already closed if missing. Never open, close, or reopen it** — its state carries no meaning; only the log does.
48	- Log each run as a **dated comment** — not a sub-issue, so history accumulates in one scrollable feed — the date, and per lesson: the origin repo, the **ladder rung it landed on** (check id / skill / owning doc, with the named reason when prose was the fallback), and the generalized rule (or, for a notable rejection, the reason and the existing rule that already covers it).
49	
50	## What this task must never do
51	
52	- **Never mine outside a local pack** — product source, task scripts, code comments, and config are out of scope; only a local pack's `RULES.md` prose and its own check modules are candidates.
53	- **Never promote a product-specific or one-off item** — it stays in that project's local packs.
54	- **Never weaken, restate, or duplicate an existing rule** — fold a genuine sharpening in per [item-routing.md](../../item-routing.md) instead.
55	- **Never widen past the Context member list**, and **never touch a member repo** — this task only reads members and writes the canon PR.
56	- **Run on `opus`** — every step is a judgment call (portability, duplication, ownership, how to generalize without distorting), and a downgraded model ships a plausible-but-wrong *acceptance* the owner's review is least likely to catch. This task declares `agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.
57
